channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Marine
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Investigators reportedly found hackers briefly reached a US-bound tanker’s propulsion system; the FBI reports no disruption
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 2 October, citing US officials not authorized to speak publicly, that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found outsiders had gained temporary access to digital systems aboard the supertanker VL Prosperity, including its propulsion system, as it approached Texas this summer. How long the access lasted and what the intruders could control is unclear, and neither agency has confirmed the propulsion finding on the record; the Coast Guard declined to comment. The FBI’s on-record statement says there are no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental harm. In September, Coast Guard Rear Adm. Amy Grable said investigators found evidence of a malicious cyber actor after assessing the ship’s IT and onboard systems. VL Prosperity was boarded on 21 August in the Atlantic and a second tanker on 24 August in the Gulf of Mexico, per Dragos; no attacker has been named. Bloomberg adds that by September US agencies were tracking cyber threats against nearly 20 vessels worldwide. Engine-speed and cooling claims come only from Iranian media and remain unverified, as does a crew claim that hackers seized tank-pressure controls on the LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG, which Italy’s Coast Guard recorded as a cargo-monitoring malfunction. - Bloomberg, 2 Oct 2026, citing unnamed US officials (via gCaptain, 5 Oct); FBI statement; Coast Guard (Rear Adm. Grable, via CBS News); Dragos, 24 Sep (boarding locations); Splash247 (Vivit Africa crew claim) - Boardings 21 & 24 Aug 2026; propulsion-access report 2 Oct; no agency confirmation of that finding as of 6 Oct

item.title: [High] Port of Tanjung Pelepas restarted in phases after a cyber incident halted container operations
item.description: A cyber incident detected late on 9 September forced Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), a joint venture of MMC Group and APM Terminals, to suspend container-terminal operations as a precaution; the terminal operating systems were affected. A phased restart began on 10 September with manual processing for export container gate-ins, and a PTP statement reported by WorldCargo News on 15 September said container operations had resumed with system recovery “advancing steadily.” The Direwolf ransomware group listed the port on its leak site on 11 September, claiming about 200 GB of data (per ransomware.live); PTP has not confirmed ransomware or any group, so that remains a claim. No newer development was found for this 6 October edition. - WorldCargo News, 15 Sep 2026, quoting PTP (primary statement); Direwolf listing via ransomware.live, 11 Sep (claim) - Incident 9 Sep 2026; phased restart from 10 Sep; operations resumed per 15 Sep statement

item.title: [Critical] Cisco Secure FMC, a common firewall console at IT/OT boundaries, remains under active exploitation
item.category: Incident — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco Talos tracks three clusters exploiting Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center flaws. UAT-12197 used CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0), an authentication bypass, to deploy web shells. UAT-11823, which Talos says overlaps in tooling with Sandworm, used both flaws and deployed a Cyclops Blink implant. UAT-11988, a ransomware operator, used CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3), which Talos says can be chained for privilege escalation, then set up proxy and SSH tunnels and deployed Qilin. Talos names no victims, sectors or countries, and its post was last updated 21 September. Editorial assessment: FMC often manages the firewalls between corporate IT and terminal-operating-system, crane and gate networks at ports. - Cisco Talos analysis, published 9 Sep 2026, last updated 21 Sep 2026 (primary); The Hacker News, 11 Sep 2026 - Exploitation confirmed early Sep 2026; no new development found after the 21 Sep update

item.title: [Medium] ENISA: China-nexus intrusion sets showed continuous interest in transport, including maritime entities
item.category: Threat Intelligence — EU threat landscape, maritime espionage interest
item.description: The EU cybersecurity agency’s Threat Landscape 2026 report, covering calendar 2025 and published 22–23 September, says China-nexus intrusion sets showed continuous interest in the transport sector, including maritime entities, per Industrial Cyber’s summary. Transport ranked fourth among the most-affected sectors at 8%. Ransomware remained the most damaging threat, and 60% of unauthorized-access incidents leveraged known vulnerabilities. The report describes long-running intelligence-collection interest rather than a specific new operation against ships or ports, and it does not name a vessel or terminal victim. - ENISA Threat Landscape 2026 (22 Sep 2026), reported by Industrial Cyber, 23 Sep 2026 - Covers 1 Jan–31 Dec 2025; published 22–23 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] FDD report: Chinese-operated port terminals and patchy cyber oversight expose NATO’s European mobility corridors
item.category: Research — Port ownership and NATO military mobility
item.description: A Foundation for Defense of Democracies report by Jiwon Ma, published 28 September, argues that foreign ownership and fragmented cyber oversight weaken the ports, railways and roads NATO would use to move forces across Europe. It says Chinese state-linked firms hold stakes in more than 30 European port terminals and, citing a 2023 European Parliament study, that COSCO Shipping, China Merchants and Hutchison Port Holdings own or operate terminals in roughly half of the EU ports considered critical to NATO. It also finds that civilian transport operators lack consistent security standards across NATO, EU and national authorities, and recommends tighter EU investment screening plus authentication and alternative navigation procedures against satellite interference. The “state-linked” characterization is FDD’s; the report describes structural exposure, not an intrusion at any port. - FDD report, 28 Sep 2026 (primary; registration required to download); Industrial Cyber, 30 Sep 2026 - Published 28 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] Honeywell survey: 87% of maritime respondents reported a significant OT incident in the past year
item.description: Honeywell’s 2026 OT Cybersecurity Benchmark, published 22 September and based on more than 600 industrial security leaders worldwide, found that 87% of maritime respondents reported a significant OT cybersecurity incident in the past 12 months, and 40% of maritime respondents named outdated equipment as their main obstacle. Across all sectors only 21% kept a complete OT asset inventory and average downtime from major incidents was 16.2 hours. This is a vendor survey of self-reported incidents; definitions of “significant” vary and it identifies no specific vessel or port. - Honeywell press release, 22 Sep 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber - Published 22 Sep 2026; survey of 600+ respondents

item.title: [Critical] Citrix NetScaler: a third exploited zero-day joins KEV, and patching alone does not evict intruders
item.description: Citrix patched two exploited NetScaler ADC and Gateway zero-days on 27 September, both CVSS 9.5 (v4): CVE-2026-88771, unauthenticated command execution that affects all deployments including the default configuration, and CVE-2026-88772, a memory overflow on appliances with DTLS enabled, the default on VPN virtual servers. CISA added both to KEV that day and says exploitation is global. On 3 October Citrix patched a third flaw, CVE-2026-88779 (CVSS 8.7), which affects only SAML SP or IdP configurations, after observing targeted attacks; CISA added it to KEV on 4 October with a 7 October deadline. Citrix and watchTowr describe it as a crash (denial-of-service) bug; one researcher reported signs of code execution, which watchTowr disputes. Responders have found web shells, a rogue admin account and stolen configuration files, and Mandiant attributes the activity only to suspected state-sponsored actors. Victim counts differ by tracker: Mandiant says dozens of organizations, Arctic Wolf at least 78, researcher Kevin Beaumont over 100. Editorial assessment: NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door into port, terminal and OT DMZ networks. - Citrix bulletins CTX697096 (27 Sep) and CTX697174 (3 Oct); CISA KEV (27 Sep, 4 Oct); Tenable FAQ, updated 4 Oct; watchTowr via SecurityWeek, 5 Oct; victim counts via Cybersecurity Dive and Help Net Security - First zero-days patched 27 Sep 2026; third added to KEV 4 Oct; federal deadline 7 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Toptech TMS7 and TopHAT: ten flaws up to CVSS 10.0 in terminal-management software, fixed in release 7.8
item.category: Advisory — Terminal-management software, CVSS 10.0, fix available
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-02 (29 September) covers ten vulnerabilities in Toptech Systems TMS7 and TopHAT 7.6.3. The most severe, CVE-2026-71379 (CVSS 10.0), leaves files and directories accessible to external parties; CVE-2026-70356 (9.1) allows unrestricted file upload, and five SQL-injection flaws score 9.0. CISA says exploitation could let an attacker access critical data or execute arbitrary code, and lists the Energy, Chemical and Transportation Systems sectors, with deployments worldwide. Toptech notified customers on 20 July and fixed all the issues in release 7.8. CISA reports no known public exploitation. Editorial assessment: Toptech’s terminal-management software is used at fuel and bulk-liquid terminals, including those in ports, so marine terminal operators should check whether they run it. - CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-02, 29 Sep 2026 (primary; CSAF via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup) - Advisory 29 Sep 2026; vendor notice to customers 20 Jul 2026; fixed in 7.8

item.title: [High] Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard hard-coded keys: CISA advisory names two CVEs and the fixed build
item.category: Advisory — Hard-coded cryptographic keys, fix available, no known exploitation
item.description: CISA’s advisory ICSA-26-258-02 (15 September) covers two hard-coded cryptographic key flaws (CWE-321) in Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard 5.07.0923.01, a shipboard fleet-optimization system: CVE-2026-81855 in its robot testing framework and CVE-2026-78225 in its deployer-ng Update Controller. CISA’s 15 September advisory rated them 9.1 and 9.0 (CVSS v3.1, network attack vector), but the published scores have differed between sources since, so check the current advisory for the rating. Per CISA, an attacker could deliver an unauthorized update, execute code or extract credentials. The fix is 5.08.4052.01, obtained through Wärtsilä’s FOS download site or patch-deployment service; the CVE records were updated on 24 September to point there. Wärtsilä says the flaws are not exploitable when the product is installed as recommended, and Cydome, which reported them, credits the vendor with a patch. No exploitation has been reported. A hard-coded key is shared across installations, so one recovered key could work fleet-wide. - CISA advisory ICSA-26-258-02, 15 Sep 2026 (primary; CSAF via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup); CVE records (CNA: ICS-CERT), updated 24 Sep 2026; Hellenic Shipping News (Cydome finding) - Advisory published 15 Sep 2026; CVE references updated 24 Sep; fixed version 5.08.4052.01

item.title: [Medium] Lantronix G520 cellular gateways: a leaked signing key lets attackers push trusted firmware; update to 2.6.0.7R6
item.category: Advisory — Cellular gateway update-signing flaw, fix available
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-01 (29 September) covers two flaws in Lantronix G520 Series cellular gateways running 2.6.0.4R6_stable, each CVSS 7.5 (v3.1). CVE-2026-91191 is a signature-verification failure in the update mechanism: per the advisory, the publicly distributed SDK contains the production private key, so an attacker could sign malicious packages the gateway will trust. CVE-2026-84409 is a cross-site scripting flaw in how the web interface displays update metadata fetched over plain HTTP. CISA says exploitation could let an attacker replace software and run code with root privileges, and lists Transportation Systems, Energy and Water and Wastewater among affected sectors. Lantronix fixed both in firmware 2.6.0.7R6; no exploitation has been reported. Editorial assessment: cellular gateways like these often link remote port-side equipment and terminal sensors back to control centers. - CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-01, 29 Sep 2026 (primary; CSAF via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup) - Advisory 29 Sep 2026; fixed in 2.6.0.7R6

item.title: [High] CISA and the FBI name transportation among sectors exposed through a compromised ICS integrator
item.category: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrator remote access
item.description: A joint FBI/CISA fact sheet on working with third-party ICS integrators, published 24 September, describes foreign cyber actors who compromised a US industrial automation company in March–April 2025 and created nine .zip files of about 800 files, including SCADA-related data, for presumed exfiltration. It names power utilities and transportation among the affected customers. It urges least privilege for integrators, secured remote-access points, offline backups and cybersecurity terms in contracts. Editorial assessment: shipyards, OEMs and other service providers often hold standing remote access to vessel and terminal control systems, so the guidance applies directly to marine operators. - FBI/CISA fact sheet, published 24 Sep 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber, 24 Sep 2026 - Cites a March–April 2025 intrusion at a US automation integrator

item.title: [Info] NIST’s draft SP 800-82 Rev. 4 brings maritime vessels into its OT security guide; comments close 30 November
item.category: Guidance — Draft OT security guide now covers maritime vessels
item.description: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, its Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security, on 21 September. The revision expands coverage to maritime vessels, building automation, water and wastewater, and freight rail, and reorganizes the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, moving risk management under the Govern function and adding Risk Management Framework appendices. It also strengthens asset-management and network-monitoring guidance and adds zero-trust architecture material, reflecting IIoT and cloud connections into OT. Comments are due 30 November 2026. This is voluntary draft guidance; for US-regulated vessels and facilities, the Coast Guard’s MTSA cybersecurity rule sets the binding requirements. - NIST CSRC, SP 800-82 Rev. 4 initial public draft, 21 Sep 2026 (primary) - Released 21 Sep 2026; comment period closes 30 Nov 2026
